why: Registered before any held-out result was produced. Everything a result could be tuned against is fixed here: what is held out, what counts as a hit, which bindings are the easy ones, and what the system has to beat. Exploratory work done before this point was on cross-game stability of the corpus as a whole, never on a held-out prediction.

corpus.author: Silas P.
corpus.what: Every profile this author has published in the official community catalog, the same list the shipped app's Community Profiles window shows.
corpus.hashes: agent/corpus/silas/bindings.json carries a sha256 per file
corpus.read_by: tools/qsf inspect, which is the shipped app's own parser

split.unit: game family, never a single file
split.why: Cyberpunk has three files and Call of Duty eight. Rebuilding one variant while holding its siblings is copying, not personalising.
split.rule: The FAMILIES table in agent/index_corpus.py, applied before any result was seen.
split.protocol: leave-one-family-out over every family in the corpus
split.held_out_families: all of them, in turn. No family is chosen, so none can be chosen for being easy.
split.training_set: every profile whose family differs from the held-out family
split.leakage_guard: The held-out profile's own cells are never read by the predictor. Only its list of output tokens is used, to ask what the system would bind each one to.

binding_classes.why: A profile is mostly rig setup that never changes between games. Scoring it together with the game's actual buttons would report a high number that means nothing.

rig.definition: output token is the joystick-to-mouse mapping, a mouse or deflection tuning value, or the mode switch
rig.expectation: close to fully predictable, and reported separately for exactly that reason

binding_classes.gameplay: every other output token. This is the headline.

metrics.unit: one output token in the held-out profile, with the physical inputs and the function keyword bound to it
metrics.inputs_compared: as an ordered tuple, because several inputs on a row are a sequence and not a set
metrics.top1_exact: predicted inputs AND function keyword both match the held-out profile
metrics.coverage: share of the held-out profile's output tokens the system predicted anything at all for
metrics.abstention: share it declined to predict. Declining is not counted as a miss; it is counted here.
metrics.headline: macro-averaged top1_exact over gameplay bindings, averaged per family so a 550-binding profile cannot outweigh a 60-binding one
metrics.not_used: raw cell equality against the held-out file, which these profiles' boilerplate would inflate
metrics.amended_2026-08-14: A review found that dropping function parameters was not only a scoring choice, it was happening in the pipeline: a habit read out of the corpus as `delay_on 500 16000` was being written as `delay_on`, deleting a timing the author set. The pipeline now carries the whole function. Two consequences are reported rather than absorbed. First, a `with timings` column was ADDED: same rows, scored with parameters, global 53.2% and nearest 42.6%. It is the stricter and more meaningful number. Second, the registered `top1_exact` itself moved from 58.1% to 57.9%, because the global baseline now picks its most common answer over whole functions rather than keywords. The registered definition is unchanged and the 0.2 point drop is reported as a drop.

baselines.global: for each output token, the inputs and function this author uses most often across the training profiles
baselines.nearest: copy the single training profile sharing the most output tokens with the held-out one
baselines.bar: the agent has to beat BOTH. An agent that cannot beat copying the closest profile you already own has added nothing.

agent_sample.why: Baselines run over all families for free. The agent costs a model call per step, so it runs on a sample.
agent_sample.chosen_by: random.Random(seed).sample of the family list sorted alphabetically, drawn at run time from this seed and reported in full

what_this_does_not_claim: That the held-out profile is the only correct configuration. It is what one expert built at one time.
That a firmware-valid profile is a usable one. Validity is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.
That any accuracy figure here predicts whether this author would accept the result. Only he can say that.
